subject: Web Development
title: npm and the Package Revolution
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on npm and the Package Revolution.

hook.text: Before npm, sharing JavaScript code meant copying files from someone's blog.

buildup.text: npm launched in 2010 as a package manager for Node.js — one command to install any library.

discovery.text: By 2020, npm hosted over one million packages. It became the largest code registry on Earth.

twist.text: Deep dependency trees meant a single broken package could cascade and break thousands of apps.

climax.text: The left-pad incident in 2016 proved it: 11 lines of deleted code broke the entire internet.

punchline.text: Convenience created a fragile dependency chain.

quiz.question: What happened in the left-pad incident?
options: 11 lines of deleted code broke the internet
npm's servers went down for a week
A virus spread through npm packages
